description: Duplicate committed record or duplicate operation key.
rationale: This is a storage-level uniqueness/idempotency violation.

description: A transition references a dependency that does not exist.
rationale: This is a storage-level referential-integrity violation.

description: A proposal attempts an illegal FSM transition.
rationale: A TP substrate can enforce this only if the application encodes the FSM rule; workflow guardrails and ATP naturally check it.

description: A generated proposal assumes facts no longer true in StateView.
rationale: Generic TP executes submitted transactions; ATP checks proposal world assumptions against effective state before authority is granted.

description: A compensation would make effective dependents orphaned.
rationale: A saga may run local compensation but need not check effective-state dependency closure unless the application encodes it.

description: A repair hides the evidence that triggered the repair.
rationale: Evidence preservation is an ATP-specific admission rule: a repair must resolve the failure or preserve the triggering evidence.

description: An active commitment wakeup mutates domain truth directly.
rationale: ATP treats ACR wakeups as non-authoritative; they may only emit proposal packages that re-enter admission.

description: Two individually plausible proposals conflict over one scope.
rationale: TP can serialize rows, but generative conflict scopes are an ATP authority-level declaration over proposal semantics.

description: A duplicate provider call or outbox intent is generated.
rationale: Outbox/idempotency can partially catch duplicates; ATP stages the intent and admits observed effects as later transitions.
